metadata.title: A Survey on Knowledge Graph-based Methods

entities.name: Knowledge Graph Embeddings
entities.description: A technique for applying machine learning to graph-structured data.
entities.context: However, recent progress in knowledge graph embeddings and graph neural networks allows to applying machine learning to graph-structured data.

entities.name: Graph Neural Networks
entities.description: A type of neural network that can be applied to graph-structured data.
entities.context: However, recent progress in knowledge graph embeddings and graph neural networks allows to applying machine learning to graph-structured data.

entities.name: Automated Driving
entities.description: The use of computer science and artificial intelligence to enable vehicles to drive autonomously.
entities.context: Abstract. Automated driving is one of the most active research areas in computer science.

entities.name: Knowledge Graphs
entities.description: A theoretical framework for modeling temporally contextualized observations and Recurrent Transformers (RETRA) for neural encoder stack with feedback loop and constrained multi-headed self-attention layers.
entities.context: An approach for KG-based scene understanding was described by Werner et al. [107]. The paper proposes a KG to model temporally contextualized observations and Recurrent Transformers (RETRA), a neural encoder stack with a feedback loop and constrained multi-headed self-attention layers.

entities.name: Machine Learning
entities.description: A subfield of artificial intelligence that involves training algorithms to make predictions or take actions based on data.
entities.context: Deep learning methods have made remarkable breakthroughs in machine learning generally and in automated driving (AD) in particular.

entities.name: Ontologies
entities.description: A formal and explicit specification of a shared conceptualization.
entities.context: In computer science, on the other hand, ontologies are defined as a formal and explicit specification of a shared conceptualization [97].

entities.name: Graph Neural Network
entities.description: A method for representing knowledge using graphs.
entities.context: The use of graphs to represent knowledge has been researched for a long time.

entities.name: Explainable AI (XAI)
entities.description: A concept introduced to provide information on what the network has learned and thus be harder to interpret and validate.
entities.context: The concept of explainable AI was therefore introduced.

entities.name: Deep Learning (DL)
entities.description: A method that has made remarkable breakthroughs with significant impact on the performance of AD systems.
entities.context: Deep learning (DL) has made remarkable breakthroughs with significant impact on the performance of AD systems.

entities.name: ISO26262
entities.description: A standard that specifies strong safety requirements for automated driving systems.
entities.context: Moreover, AD systems must consider the strong safety requirements specified in ISO26262...

entities.name: Knowledge Graph (KG)
entities.description: A graph-based representation of structured facts with entities connected via named relationships.
entities.context: Thetermknowledgegraph(KG)waspopularizedwiththeannouncementoftheGoogle Knowledge Graph [95].

entities.name: Graph-Based Representation
entities.description: A concise and intuitive abstraction of knowledge with edges representing the relations that exist between entities.
entities.context: A graph-based representation has several advantages over alternative approaches to represent knowledge.

entities.name: Machine learning on graphs
entities.description: A model and comprehensive taxonomy of machine learning on graphs.
entities.context: 14. Chami,I.,Abu-El-Haija,S.,Perozzi,B.,Ré,C.,Murphy,K.:Machinelearningon graphs: A model and comprehensive taxonomy. CoRR abs/2005.03675 (2020)

entities.name: Named Relationships
entities.description: The connections between entities in a knowledge graph, representing the relations that exist between them.
entities.context: Knowledge graphs are means for structuring facts, with entities connected via named relationships.

entities.name: Factual Triple
entities.description: A format for expressing knowledge in the form of (head, relation, tail) or (subject, predicate, object).
entities.context: Knowledge can be expressed in a factual triple in the form of (head, relation, tail) or (subject, predicate, object) under the Resource Description Framework (RDF), for example, (Albert Einstein, WinnerOf, Nobel Prize).

entities.name: Resource Description Framework (RDF)
entities.description: A framework for expressing data in the form of factual triples.
entities.context: can be expressed in a factual triple in the form of (head, relation, tail) or (subject, predicate, object) under the Resource Description Framework (RDF), for example, (Albert Einstein, WinnerOf, Nobel Prize).

entities.name: Graph-based operations
entities.description: Operations used to manipulate data in graph models.
entities.context: The datamanipulation is realized by graph-based operations and adequate integrity constraints[1].

entities.name: Graph model
entities.description: A model that structures data, including its schema and/or instances in the form of graphs.
entities.context: A graph model is a model which structures the data, including its schema and/or instances in the form of graphs, and the datamanipulation is realized by graph-based operations and adequate integrity constraints[1].

entities.name: Directed Labeled Graphs
entities.description: A type of graph model that represents data with labeled nodes and edges.
entities.context: Directed Labeled Graphs A directed labeled graph is comprised of a set of nodes and a set of edges connecting those nodes, labeled based on a specific vocabulary.

entities.name: Hyper-relational Graphs
entities.description: A type of graph model that represents data with complex relationships.
entities.context: Hyper-relational Graphs A hyper-relational graph is also a labeled directed multigraph where each node and edge might have a number of associated key-value pairs [2].

entities.name: Knowledge graph
entities.description: A type of graph data structure that represents knowledge and relationships.
entities.context: Halilaj, L., Dindorkar, I., Luettin, J., Rothermel, S.: A knowledge graph-based approach for situation comprehension in driving scenarios. In: ESWC (2021)

entities.name: Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE)
entities.description: A representation where entities and relations of a KG are mapped into low-dimensional vectors.
entities.context: Using a knowledge graph embedding method (KGE-Method), a KG can be transformed into a knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a representation where entities and relations of a KG are mapped into low-dimensional vectors.

entities.name: KGE-Method
entities.description: A graph embedding method that transforms a knowledge graph into a representation where entities and relations are mapped into low-dimensional vectors.
entities.context: ge graph em- bedding method (KGE-Method), a KG can be transformed into a knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a representation where entities and relations of a KG are mapped into low-dimensional vectors.

entities.name: Graph Embedding
entities.description: A representation where entities and relations of a graph are mapped into low-dimensional vectors.
entities.context: The KGE captures semantic meanings and relations of the graph nodes and reflects them by locality in vector space [106].

entities.name: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
entities.description: An extension of deep learning networks that can directly work on a knowledge graph.
entities.context: Common supervised KGE-Methods are based on graph neural networks (GNNs) [30], an extension of DL networks that can directly work on a KG.

entities.name: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN)
entities.description: A method for scalability and overcoming challenges that arise from graph irregularities.
entities.context: For scalability reasons and to overcome challenges that arise from graph irregularities, various adaptations have emerged such as graph convolutional networks (GCN) [60] and graph attention networks (GAT) [104].

entities.name: Graph Attention Networks (GAT)
entities.description: A method for scalability and overcoming challenges that arise from graph irregularities.
entities.context: For scalability reasons and to overcome challenges that arise from graph irregularities, various adaptations have emerged such as graph convolutional networks (GCN) [60] and graph attention networks (GAT) [104].

entities.name: deep reinforcement learning
entities.description: A machine learning approach that combines deep learning and reinforcement learning to make decisions.
entities.context: ding computer vision [53], object detection [3,31], DL based scene understanding [71,36,33,49],DLbasedvehiclebehaviorprediction [78],deepreinforcementlearning [61],lanedetection[118,79,99],semanticsegmentation[65,73],and planning and decision making [28,82,94,8,18].

entities.name: knowledge-infused learning
entities.description: An approach that incorporates knowledge graphs into machine learning models to improve their performance.
entities.context: More recently, ontologies and KGs have gained interest for knowledge-infused learning approaches.

entities.name: ontology
entities.description: A formal representation of a set of concepts and relationships used to model relevant knowledge in the automotive domain.
entities.context: Severalontologieshavebeendevelopedtomodelrelevantknowledgeintheautomotive domain.

entities.name: Scene Understanding
entities.description: Understanding what is happening in the scene, and relations between objects for further steps in automated driving.
entities.context: Scene understanding aims to understand what is happening in the scene, the relations between the objects in order to obtain a comprehension for further steps in automated driving that deal with motion planning and vehicle control.

entities.name: vehicle behavior prediction
entities.description: The ability to predict the behavior of vehicles in different scenarios.
entities.context: DLbasedvehiclebehaviorprediction [78]

entities.name: lane detection
entities.description: The process of detecting the lanes on a road.
entities.context: 79. Narote, S.P., Bhujbal, P.N., Narote, A.S., Dhane, D.M.: A review of recent advances in lane detection and departure warning system. Pattern Recognition (2018)

entities.name: semantic segmentation
entities.description: The process of assigning a semantic meaningful class label (e.g. road, sidewalk, pedestrian, road sign, vehicle) to each pixel in a given image.
entities.context: The goal of semantic segmentation is to assign a semantic meaningful class label (e.g. road, sidewalk, pedestrian, road sign, vehicle) to each pixel in a given image.

entities.name: planning and decision making
entities.description: The ability to make decisions and plan actions in complex scenarios.
entities.context: and planning and decision making [28,82,94,8,18].

entities.name: hybrid learning approach
entities.description: A method for categorizing drivers based on their driving styles.
entities.context: An ontology for modeling driver profiles based on their demographic and behavioral aspects is proposed by [89]. It is used as an input for a hybrid learning approach for categorizing drivers according to their driving styles.

entities.name: driver profiling
entities.description: A method for modeling driver profiles based on demographic and behavioral aspects.
entities.context: An ontology for modeling driver profiles based on their demographic and behavioral aspects is proposed by [89].

entities.name: automotive ontologies
entities.description: Theoretical frameworks for understanding automotive concepts, including vehicle, driver, and context.
entities.context: Table 1. Automotive ontologies. Relevant ontologies split into different categories considering their main focus and concepts.

entities.name: driver assistance ontology
entities.description: A theoretical framework for understanding driver assistance concepts, including domain understanding, decision-making, and information sharing.
entities.context: Driver Assistance An ontology for driver assistance is described in [58]. It serves as a common basis for domain understanding, decision-making, and in-formation sharing.

entities.name: traffic intersection ontology
entities.description: A theoretical framework for understanding traffic intersections, including reasoning about the right-of-way.
entities.context: Huelsen et al. [50,51] developed an ontology for traffic intersections to reason about the right-of-way

entities.name: Route Planning
entities.description: A method for modeling and processing map data in cars.
entities.context: Suryawanshi et al. [98] presented an ontology-based method for modeling and processing map data in cars.

entities.name: Ontology-Based Method
entities.description: A method for modeling and processing map data using ontologies.
entities.context: Suryawanshi et al. [98] presented an ontology-based method for modeling and processing map data in cars.

entities.name: Context Model
entities.description: An ontology for context representation and environmental modelling for AD.
entities.context: Ulbrich et al. [102] described an ontology for context representation and environmental modelling for AD.

entities.name: Automated Driving Systems Ontology
entities.description: A description of the levels of automated driving systems, ranging from fully manual to fully automated.
entities.context: An ontology describing the levels of automated driving systems, ranging from fully manual to fully automated was presented in [83].

entities.name: Automotive Urban Traffic Ontology (A.U.T.O.)
entities.description: An ontology for structured description and categorization of urban scenes in the context of automated driving.
entities.context: mprehensive 6-layer model for a structured description and categorization of urban scenes was describe in [93]. This was further developed into the Automotive Urban Traffic Ontology (A.U.T.O.) [109].

entities.name: Route Planning with Ontologies
entities.description: The use of ontologies to improve the capabilities and performance of on-board route-planning.
entities.context: Schlenoff et al. [91] explored the use of ontologies to improve the capabilities and performance of on-board route-planning.

entities.name: Semantic State Space
entities.description: A modeling approach for maneuver planning using semantic state space.
entities.context: Kohlhaas et al. [63] introduced a modeling approach for the semantic state space for maneuver planning.

entities.name: Automotive Global Ontology (AGO)
entities.description: An ontology for semantic labeling and testing use cases in the context of automated driving.
entities.context: The Automotive Global Ontology(AGO) [103] focuses on semantic labeling and testing use cases.

entities.name: Scene Graphs
entities.description: A technique to semantically describe and represent objects and relations in a scene.
entities.context: Scene graphs are a relatively recent technique to semantically describe and represent objects and relations in a scene [56].

entities.name: Object Detection
entities.description: The detection of traffic participants such as vehicles, pedestrians, road markings, traffic signs, and others.
entities.context: Object detection in AD includes the detection of traffic participants such as vehicles, pedestrians, road markings, traffic signs, and others.

entities.name: Bottom-up Approach
entities.description: An approach to object detection that consists of object detection followed by pairwise relationship recognition.
entities.context: The first, bottom up approach, consists of object detection followed by pairwise relationship recognition.

entities.name: Top-down Approach
entities.description: An approach to object detection that consists of joint detection and recognition of objects and their relationships.
entities.context: The second, top-down approach, consists of joint detection and recognition of objects and their relationships.

entities.name: bottom up approach
entities.description: A method that consists of object detection followed by pairwise relationship recognition.
entities.context: The second, top-down approach, consists of joint detection and recognition of objects and their relationships.

entities.name: top down approach
entities.description: A method that consists of joint detection and recognition of objects and their relationships.
entities.context: The second, top-down approach, consists of joint detection and recognition of objects and their relationships.

entities.name: Graph Bridging Networks (GB-Net)
entities.description: A method that regards the scene graph as the image conditioned instantiation of the commonsense knowledge graph.
entities.context: The use of KGs to provide background knowledge and generate scene graphs is recently proposed [114] with Graph Bridging Networks (GB-Net).

entities.name: ConceptNet
entities.description: Practical commonsense reasoning toolkit.
entities.context: Liu,H.,Singh,P.: Conceptnet—apracticalcommonsensereasoningtool-kit.BT Technology Journal 22, 211–226 (2004)

entities.name: KB-GAN
entities.description: A method that uses external knowledge and image reconstruction loss to overcome problems found in datasets.
entities.context: Gu et al. [34] presented KB-GAN, a knowledge base and auxiliary image generation approach based on external knowledge and image reconstruction loss to overcome the problems found in datasets.

entities.name: knowledge graph embedding
entities.description: A method for representing and processing knowledge graphs.

entities.name: object detection as a KG link prediction problem
entities.description: A theoretical framework that formalizes object detection as a KG link prediction problem.
entities.context: This is accomplished with a novel mapping and formalization of object detection as a KG link prediction problem.

entities.name: KGE algorithms evaluation
entities.description: A method that evaluates several KGE algorithms and compares them.
entities.context: Several KGE algorithms are evaluated and compared [110].

entities.name: global context encoding
entities.description: A method that extracts global context information using a geometric layout encoding.
entities.context: Woo et al. [112] presented a method to embed relations by jointly learning connections between objects. It contains a global context encoding and a geometric layout encoding which extract global context information and spatial information.

entities.name: road sign detection
entities.description: A use case that focuses on using knowledge-graphs for road sign detection.
entities.context: Road-Sign Detection Several approaches focus on using knowledge-graphs for road sign detection [59,76].

entities.name: knowledge graph neural network (KG-NN)
entities.description: A method that uses a knowledge graph neural network to supervise the training using image-data-invariant auxiliary knowledge.
entities.context: Monka et al. [76] proposed an approach for object recognition based on a knowledge graph neural network (KG-NN) that supervises the training using image-data-invariant auxiliary knowledge.

entities.name: KG-NN
entities.description: A knowledge graph neural network that supervises the training using image-data-invariant auxiliary knowledge.
entities.context: a knowledge graph neural network (KG-NN) that supervises the training using image-data-invariantauxiliaryknowledge.

entities.name: embedding method
entities.description: A method for transforming KG with respective concepts and their relationships into a dense vector representation.
entities.context: These are transformed into a dense vector representation by an embedding method.

entities.name: contrastive loss function
entities.description: A method for adapting the visual embedding space of KG-NN.
entities.context: The KG-NN learns to adapt its visual embedding space by a contrastive loss function.

entities.name: graph-embedding-based approach
entities.description: A method for lane detection that uses graph embeddings.
entities.context: A graph-embedding-based approach for lane detection [72] can robustly detect parallel, non-parallel (merging or splitting), varying lane width, and partially blocked lane markings.

entities.name: lane features

entities.context: A novel graph structure is used to represent lane features, lane geometry, and lane topology.

entities.name: scene graph
entities.description: A logical representation that models the structure of the road using an abstract representation.
entities.context: A scene graph is generated from a set of segmented entities that models the structure of the road using an abstract, logical representation to enable the incorporation of background knowledge.

entities.name: Recurrent Transformers
entities.description: A neural encoder stack with a feedback loop and constrained multi-headed self-attention layers for modeling temporally contextualized observations.

The paper proposes a KG to model temporally contextualized observations and Recurrent Transformers (RETRA), a neural encoder stack with a feedback loop and constrained multi-headed self-attention layers.

entities.name: Digital Maps

relationships.context: The paper discusses graph neural networks as a type of deep learning technique for processing graph-structured data.
RETRA enables transformation of global KG-embeddings into custom embeddings, given the situation-specific factors of the relation and the subjective history of the entity.
The paper is based on the idea that knowledge graphs can be used to represent ontological knowledge in the context of automated driving.

Scene understanding aims to understand what is happening in the scene, the relations between the objects in order to obtain a comprehension for further steps in automated driving that deal with motion planning and vehicle control.
The model builds on the terminology of [101] and uses existing ontologies such as SOSA [54].
